summary: Bruce M. Sullivan is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

Bruce Matthews works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. A graduate alumnus of McMaster University, he was a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Ceylon and served as C. B. Lumsden Professor of Comparative Religion at Acadia University (~1976–2006).

Bruce McCoy Owens is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held posts at Columbia University (attested 1988) and Wheaton College, where he was attested in 2019 as associate professor of anthropology.

Bruno Dagens (1935–2023) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Colette Caillat and held positions at EFEO, Catholic University of Louvain, French Institute of Pondicherry, KU Leuven (~1977–1986), and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1986).
Bruno Galasek specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich (1862–1939) was an Indologist. He studied under Franz Kielhorn at Göttingen, completed his Habilitation at Breslau, and studied at Munich. He held posts at the University of Breslau (1921–1928) and Heidelberg University (~1921–1939).

Bruno Lindner (1853–1930) specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig University and under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as a Privatdozent at Leipzig University from 1878 to 1919.

Bruno Petzold (1873–1949) studied at Leipzig and Berlin, and under Hikoshiro Hoshino and Daito Shimaji. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, he taught at First Higher School (1917–1943), Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei High School.

Bruno Schindler (1882–1964) was a Sinologist who completed his doctorate under August Conrady (~1912–1919). He founded Asia Major in 1923 and served as a Verlagslektor at Lund Humphries from ~1939 to 1964.

Bryan D. Lowe specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Otani University and under mentors including Jacqueline I. Stone and Martin Collcutt, holding a post at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017).

Bryan J. Cuevas specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Emory and the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, he was a Princeton postdoctoral fellow and became the John F. Priest Professor at Florida State University.

Bryan W. Van Norden is a scholar of philosophy and Sinology. He studied at Stanford University (~1985–1991) and held a professorship in philosophy and Chinese & Japanese at Vassar College starting around 1996.
Bryce Ryan (1911–1993) was a scholar in Indology and other fields. Over his career, he held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Ceylon.

Bulcsu Siklós is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles Roskelly Bawden, and later held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1996).

Bunkyo Aoki (1886–1956) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University, was a disciple of Kozui Otani (~1909–1914), and was appointed as a lecturer in Tibetan at the University of Tokyo in 1951.

Bunsaku Kurata (1918–1983) studied at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda universities, working in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. He served at the Tokyo National Museum, National Commission for the Protection of Cultural Properties, and became Nara National Museum Director in 1975.

Bunyiu Nanjio (1849–1927), a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, studied at Oxford under Max Müller. He taught at the University of Tokyo and served as head of Otani University and rector of Ryukoku University (~1914–1923).

Bunzaburo Matsumoto (1869–1944) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He taught at Rikkyo University, First Higher School, and Kyoto University, serving as Kyoto's second president (1908–1915).

Burchard Brentjes (1929–2012) worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Heinz Adolf Mode, later holding a post there from ~1954 to 1978.

Burkhard Quessel specializes in Tibetology and Indology. He studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was a member (attested 1997), and worked as a curator at the British Library (attested 2002–2012).
